decisions.reason: The reference-class electrometer is a flagship product at the core of the firm's dosimetry business, has been featured on the home page in both years, and costs little to keep, so keeping the option open clearly pays.

Oncology risk management software lies further from the core measurement business and its value is still uncertain, but carrying software on the market costs little and it fits the firm's integration and prediction strategy, so the option stays open.
The CT image quality phantom was launched only in 2024 and is a low-cost physical product that supports the firm's push into imaging QA, so it is far too early to abandon it.
The mammography image phantom is newly launched with unresolved prospects and little holding cost, though its overlap with Product E makes later consolidation somewhat possible.
The full-field mammography phantom is a recent, inexpensive addition to the imaging QA line whose value has not yet been revealed, so keeping it preserves the option.
The imaging QA instrument line is a flagship of the firm's new direction and an anchor for the expanding imaging portfolio, so the firm commits to it rather than dropping it.
